text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) usually has no symptoms at all, which is why it is widely known as the "silent killer".
When blood pressure is very high or rises quickly, some people may notice mild or easy-to-miss signs:

list.snippet: Headaches: Persistent or early-morning dull head pain.
Vision changes: Blurry vision or eye strain.
Shortness of breath: Getting winded easily during light activity.
Fatigue or confusion: Feeling unusually tired or unfocused.
Pounding or racing heartbeat: Heart palpitations or pulsing in the ears and neck.

text_blocks.snippet: Blood pressure readings above 180/120 mm Hg can signal a dangerous crisis. Seek emergency medical care immediately if extremely high blood pressure is accompanied by:

list.snippet: Severe, sudden chest pain or tightness
Sudden severe headache unlike past headaches
Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Stroke signs: Numbness, weakness on one side, facial drooping, or trouble speaking
Sudden vision loss or severe changes
Confusion or sudden severe back/abdominal pain

text_blocks.snippet: To verify your levels safely, check the guidance provided by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention or read more from the Cleveland Clinic.
